title: The Wild Wolf
premise: In the valley of Vaelmoor, where an ancient ward suppresses all magic, Noor Kavanagh has spent her life hiding the fact that she can speak with beasts—a gift the usurper King Aldric has made punishable by death. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin to be answered, Noor learns she is the last living heir of the Wolf Covenant, the pact that once bound human, beast, and god into one law. Hunted by Aldric's inquisitors and guided by a found family of outcasts—a disgraced knight, a runaway priest, and a wolf who is more than a wolf—she must journey to the shattered Godstone and reforge the covenant before Aldric's armies crush the free cities. In the end, Noor chooses to bind herself to the covenant as its living voice, sacrificing her anonymity and her chance at an ordinary life, but winning a new law that no king can own.
about_author: Bram Nakamura is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who grew up between rural Ireland and coastal Japan, and whose love of animal behavior seeps into every page. They write fantasy about outsiders, old debts, and the voices we're told not to hear, and live somewhere with too many raincoats for one person.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the magic-dead valley of Vaelmoor, Noor secretly tends a wounded wolf, speaking to it in a voice she must never let anyone hear. When an inquisitor's patrol arrives asking about 'beast-speakers,' she realizes her valley's safety is an illusion. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a hidden life cracking open.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The old gods stir: crops fail in patterns, animals flee the valley, and the wolf—named Fen—speaks her name aloud, which should be impossible inside the ward. Fen tells her the covenant is breaking and she is its heir. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror as her invisibility dies.

chapters.title: Ash on the Border Stone
chapters.summary: Knight's POV. Ser Ivo Marchetti, a disgraced knight fleeing Aldric's purge, reaches the valley's edge and finds the ward burning away. He warns Noor's village that inquisitors will come for anyone touched by the old magic. Emotional beat: a broken man choosing, for once, to warn rather than save himself.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Fen shares inherited memory: the Wolf Covenant, the Godstone, and Aldric's betrayal of it years ago. Noor's mentor is seized by inquisitors as bait. Emotional beat: grief and guilt—her secret has a body count—and the resolve that follows.

chapters.title: Outcasts' Road
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor and Ivo. Noor flees with Fen and Ivo, joined by Sela, a runaway priestess of the old gods. They evade a checkpoint using Noor's gift to turn a mule train's animals. Emotional beat: wary strangers becoming, grudgingly, a band.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Mercy
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The king, once the covenant's sworn guardian, justifies his purge: he saw the gods as tyrants and broke their law to free mankind, and now hunts the heir to undo his mistake. Emotional beat: chilling, sympathetic villainy—conviction mistaken for justice.

chapters.title: River of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. The band follows a river where minor spirits are waking, and Sela's abandoned faith is tested when the spirits demand a price for passage. Noor negotiates with them as she negotiates with beasts. Emotional beat: Sela learning that faith is a relationship, not a refuge.

chapters.title: The Godstone Broken
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the shattered Godstone, the band finds the inquisitors waiting; Ivo falls holding the pass so Noor can reach the stone, and she learns reforging the covenant requires a willing voice to speak for all three realms. Emotional beat: devastating loss and the weight of a choice she cannot refuse.

chapters.title: A Law of Teeth and Mercy
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. As Aldric's army arrives at the stone, Noor speaks the covenant, binding beast, god, and human law—and Aldric's own oath from his guardian days turns against him. Fen takes the god-wolf's form at her side. Emotional beat: the climax—Noor trading her old life for a new law, spoken in a voice no one can silence.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, months later. Magic returns to Vaelmoor; the free cities hold under the covenant's protection, and Noor returns home not as the hidden girl but as the covenant's living voice, with Sela and Fen beside her and Ivo's shield nailed above her door. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging—found family, inherited burden, and peace hard-won.
